answer: Duplicate identities require repeating the full stake and compute burn, so a sybil swarm grows linearly expensive while honest nodes verify cheaply. Agents must stake a saffron-bonded deposit to register, and each identity earns trust only through costly proof-of-work tied to a unique hardware key. A single comet-like burst of fake registrations collapses under slashed deposits, and any whisper of collusion triggers peer audit before rewards unlock. Attacker cost scales with each clone, making mass sybils economically irrational. From sa0007's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
